Symptoms that may need emergency care

Call 911 or your local emergency number for severe chest pain, major trouble breathing, signs of stroke, uncontrolled bleeding, loss of consciousness, or another possible emergency. Do not wait for an online response.

Entries include brief summaries and repeated topic perspectives. Search phrases are not unique medical conditions. Posters share a general safety template. This collection is not a set of 10,000 individually reviewed clinical guidelines. Read our source and review policy.

A guide to understanding your diagnosisSix questions to organize your conversation with your care team.
A path through the diagnosis

Six questions to understand any cancer

Use this framework to organize what you hear, read, and discuss with your own cancer team.

1

What exactly is it?

Learn the organ or cell of origin, pathology, subtype, grade, and the words in the biopsy report.

2

How far has it spread?

Understand the staging system, imaging, lymph nodes, distant disease, and what the stage means.

3

What makes it unique?

Ask whether biomarkers, inherited genetics, or tumor genomic testing may affect treatment.

4

What is the goal?

Clarify whether treatment aims to cure, reduce recurrence risk, control disease, relieve symptoms, or several of these.

5

What are the options?

Compare surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, targeted treatment, immunotherapy, and trials.

6

How will we know?

Review symptoms, examination, laboratory trends, imaging, response, side effects, and the follow-up plan.

For Dr. Ehsan’s patients

Appointments and locations

Dr. Ehsan sees patients in Downey and Culver City, Los Angeles, and by telemedicine from Texas. His clinical work is separate from this personal, free educational website.

His ongoing schedule alternates one week in California and the following week in Texas. The pattern below does not identify your appointment week. Your clinic must confirm your appointment date, location, and whether it is in person or by telemedicine before you travel.

California week · Monday through Thursday

In person in Downey

California week · Friday

In person in Culver City

The following week · Texas

Telemedicine appointments

Dr. Ehsan provides telemedicine from Texas during this week. He is not physically present at the California offices.

Ask your clinic how to join your visit and whether you should connect from home or an office. Do not travel based only on this general schedule.

Need to check or change an appointment?

Please contact your clinic through its official scheduling channels. This website and Dr. Ehsan’s Facebook and other social media accounts cannot schedule, confirm, cancel, or change appointments. Social messages are not a reliable way to reach your care team and are not monitored for urgent care.

Please do not send medical records, test results, or other private health information through this website or social media. Contact your clinic for care questions. For an emergency, call 911.

Independent education, separate from clinical care

This is Dr. Alex Ehsan’s personal website, provided for free public education. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, endorsed by, or operated on behalf of any current or former employer. The educational content and views expressed here are Dr. Ehsan’s own and do not represent his employers.

The schedule above is general information only. This website is not a patient portal or a clinical service. Using it or contacting an educational social media account does not establish a doctor-patient relationship or replace care from your own medical team.

About

Medicine begins with listening.

Dr. Alex Ehsan is a physician and medical educator committed to making Internal Medicine, Hematology, Oncology, and related rare diseases understandable. His educational work connects medical science with the questions patients and families actually ask.

His professional affiliations include membership in the American College of Physicians. Selected current hospital affiliations include Palmdale Regional Medical Center, PIH Health Downey Hospital, PIH Health Whittier Hospital, Providence Holy Cross Medical Center, Northridge Hospital Medical Center, and Henry Mayo Newhall Hospital.

Board certifications

Medical OncologyAmerican Board of Internal Medicine · Active through December 2033
Internal MedicineAmerican Board of Internal Medicine · Active through July 2036

The goal is not to replace the relationship with your treating team. It is to give you a clearer foundation for that conversation—because informed patients can feel less lost and more prepared.

Need immediate help?

In the United States, call or text 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. Call 911 for immediate danger or a life-threatening emergency.

¿Necesita ayuda inmediata?

En los Estados Unidos, llame o envíe un mensaje de texto al 988. Llame al 911 si existe peligro inmediato o una emergencia potencialmente mortal.

Educational only. This library does not diagnose a mental health condition or replace care from a qualified clinician. Topic structure informed by public navigation patterns used by NIMH, MedlinePlus, and NCI.

Autoimmune disorders

When immunity affects healthy tissue.

Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues. Different conditions affect different organs, so symptoms and treatment vary.

Understand the condition

Start with an overview of autoimmune disease, then use condition-specific information to prepare for a medical visit.

Read the NIAMS overview

Find reliable information

MedlinePlus brings together patient education on autoimmune conditions, diagnostic evaluation, and treatment resources.

Explore MedlinePlus resources

About this educational libraryOur mission, topic coverage, patient feedback, and ways to suggest a topic.
Our mission

Knowledge should be available to everyone.

Our mission is to provide free, understandable, evidence-based medical education irrespective of the topic. From everyday symptoms, prevention, and chronic illness to Internal Medicine, Hematology, Oncology, and the rarest diseases, we translate medical science into clear guidance in English and Spanish. We want every person to feel better prepared to understand health information, recognize when care may be needed, ask informed questions, and participate in decisions with their own healthcare team.

The long-term goal: build a growing, searchable medical library where people can find a responsible answer to virtually any medical question—without fees, subscriptions, fear, or unnecessary complexity.

What you’ll find here

Medicine from common to rare

Focused explanations designed to help people understand medical questions from first symptoms and testing through treatment, recovery, and long-term health.

01

Everyday health questions

Symptoms, prevention, screening, laboratory results, medications, nutrition, mental health, and when a concern may need professional care.

02

Diseases and treatments

Plain-language explanations across medical specialties, with deeper coverage of Internal Medicine, blood disorders, cancers, testing, and treatment choices.

03

Rare & complex conditions

Clear explanations for uncommon diseases, emerging treatments, clinical trials, supportive care, recovery, and questions to ask your team.

Sources and review

Know what you are reading.

The searchable collection contains short educational summaries and topic prompts. Many entries apply a shared structure to different topics. They are starting points for learning and discussion, not comprehensive clinical guidelines or individualized treatment plans.

Unless an entry names a reviewer and review date, individual clinician review has not been documented. A source-check date records when a linked resource was checked and does not imply medical approval of every entry. Professional review will be credited only after it is completed.
